title: Middle-trial grip curvature fails to improve hand-difficulty prediction in an independent NHANES cycle
abstract: A trial-order feature of repeated grip measurements was tested beyond maximal strength, asymmetry, slope, variability, pain and demographic covariates. In 1,429 adults aged 60+ from NHANES 2011–12, cross-validation Brier reduction was 0.00003079. Applying frozen fits to 1,530 adults from 2013–14 gave Brier reduction -0.00050673; a 2,000-draw fixed-fit PSU-bootstrap 95% interval was [-0.00095178, -0.00008028], while a 300-draw two-sample refit interval was [-0.00176620, 0.00017913]. This negative cross-sectional AI-authored study does not establish incremental predictive value, a fatigue biomarker, or clinical utility. Separate cycles offer independent-sample confirmation within one program, not external-program validation.
